_comment: What's new cards. One key per kit version, one short line per highlight.
The installer draws a card for every version it crossed during an upgrade,
and `exakit whats-new [version]` reads the same lines. This file is the only
source: there is nothing else to keep in step.
Rules, enforced by tests/whats-new.sh so a bad line cannot reach a user:
- a line is at most 68 characters, or the card would truncate it to '...'
- at most 6 lines per version, or the card stops being skimmable
- a version key is a plain dotted number (0.2.0), because the installer
sorts them to decide which cards a jump like 0.1.0 -> 0.4.0 crosses
- lines stay ASCII. PowerShell 5.1 reads a BOM-less file through the
legacy ANSI codepage, so an em dash here renders as garbage on Windows
- the same trap tests/ps-encoding-guard.sh catches in .ps1 files but
cannot see in a data file
Write what the reader can now DO, not what changed in the code. A first
install shows no cards at all, so every line here is read by someone who
already had the kit working and wants to know what is different.
0.2.0: New: exakit marketplace adds dashboards, VS Code and JSON loading.
New: exakit update applies the tested version set.
New: exakit version shows installed and advertised versions.
The installer downloads 4x less: 27 MB down to 6.5 MB.
0.2.2: exakit status says installing while the installer runs.
exakit sql runs a saved file: --file <path> or stdin.
Fixes come first in exakit sql errors, on stdout.
exakit version --json and mcp-status --json return objects.
EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS=all now means the clients installed here.
A busy database port is reported as a conflict, not running.
0.2.3: EXAKIT_MCP_CLIENTS=all skips clients the kit only wrote a file for.
A client counts as installed by its program or app, not its config.
0.2.4: exakit sql --json returns one object: rows, or error plus remedy.
exakit status --json names a remedy for each unfinished step.
mcp-doctor blames only the client whose config drifted.
mcp-setup re-offers a client whose config lost the kit's entry.
SELECT TOP and a busy-port TLS failure now come with a hint.
0.2.5: exakit sql --json handles any result size and reports row_count.
exakit mcp-remove <client> drops the kit's entries from a client.
mcp-doctor repairs warnings too; add-ons only reach connected clients.
Every command refuses an unknown option with exit 2, before acting.
A crashed installer no longer leaves status saying installing.
Unsupported data files are refused up front, never a failed step.
